posts.name: kreistor
posts.cooked:
I've seen some nice combos above, but they all pale in comparison to the following.

Legacy + Visionary + Absolute Zero

Absolute Zero is the lynch pin. Eveyrone will make him better.

In Play:

AZ: Isothermic Transducer, Null-Point Cailbration Unit, Focused Apertures, and the absolute mandatory Thermal Shockwave

Legacy: Inspiring Presence

Visionary: Twist the Ether (on AZ)

 

Shockwave does 3 targets 1 cold + 1 Ins Pres + 1 Galvanize + 1 TtE = 4 damage to 3 targets = 12 Cold damage dealt

Shockwave deals himself 12 Cold (TtE converts from Fire) + 1 Ins Pres + 1 Gal + 1 TtE = Heal 15 damage

 

This gets better when AZ has Cryo Chamber (+1 Heal), Cold Snap (all targets 4 damage, +4 heal per target), and Impale (5 cold to one, heal 5 more per Impale). Dealing 20+ damage and healing to full is fairly easy. The only weak point in getting this combo out is Visionary. She only has 2 TtE, so you can go the entire game looking for it. Without TtE, you still dish out damage, but one Shockwave hit needs to come back at AZ for initial healing, to soak the Fire feedback, before the transducer heals him again. Getting too aggressive without TtE putting too many of AZ's Start of Turn damage cards into play may mean you can't Shockwave more than 1 enemy, but in that case he's still dumping out massive damage.

There are characters that can pour out some damage once in a while... by blowing up their equipment (O-X), or risking their own death (Fanatic). Or their stuff is fragile (O-X takes 5). Or discarding (Bunker) or finessing the kills to one character (Haka). Only AZ can dish this kind of damage every turn, round after round, and keep his HP at max.

Ra does not play nice with AZ. He can deal him Fire, but he must never play Imbued Fire, or Absolute Zero is completely shut down, since he can no longer heal. (Also hurts Knyfe who needs her damage to be melee and energy, while Fanatic needs her damage to be Radiant.) Flesh of the Sun God can cut off Shockwave's feedback damage and Thermodynamics' fire damage.

I have yet to mix Captain Oblivious... I mean Cosmic... into that team. I suspect he will only improve it, but I need closer examination.

Omnitron-X is, for certain, the single most powerful stand-alone deck in the game right now. (Ironic that he came with the weakest deck, Chrono-ranger.) Nothing swarms cards into play like he does. He can provide Unity with Equpment to sacrifice, group heals, irreducable damage that doesn't take a Power, and takes little to recover from disaster. I do not, however, see a power combo with him, yet.

By focusing only on large instances of damage, you are completely missing the joy that is Chrono-Ranger.

Chrono-Ranger's strength isn't in his ability to wail on villains with huge shots of damage (though he can do that on occasion), but in the massive number of small shots that he can do. All of his One-Shots (more than half of his deck) allow him to ping at least one target. Some of them let him play more cards. Get his hat out and he can play even more cards. All of his One-Shots other than Terrible Tech-Strike also help him to get the things that he needs (via search, recover from trash, or extra draw). Ultimate Target lets him use extra powers out of turn - even more instances of damage.

The more instances of damage you deal, the more you benefit from damage boosting. CR does so many little shots and if he gets a damage boost, they all get boosted. In addition to whatever his allies might do for him, he's got three sources of damage boost in his deck (By Any Means, Ultimate Target, Hunter and Hunted). With just a few cards in play (e.g. Ultimate Target, Jim's Hat, Compounded Bow), Chrono-Ranger can easily be dealing 7 instances of 2 damage each round to a single target. Add another +1 boost, and he's doing 21 damage per round. This is just with a couple of cards.

Is it possible to not draw the right cards? Sure, but that's the case for every hero and Chrono-Ranger happens to have a lot of tools to find the cards that will help him.

posts.name: kreistor
posts.cooked:
Defining "killer combo" to whatever is convenient to your argument is just being argumentative.

A killer combo is a combination of cards that results in an amplifying effect that makes the group more capable as a whole than as individuals in defeating enemies. I base that on the first post, which was intended to set the stage for the discussion. He talks about "hot damage", so his intent was combinations of cards from different characters that amplify damage more than normal. I will expand that to being "more effective against the enemy" than just large damage because some enemies are not just about dealing damage... but more effective combinations in winning against a broad range of opponents.

That said, each villain is different. Some are disadvantaged by area damage, and some by direct damage. There are specific combinations that are effective against specific enemies. The best team to take against an individual villain is not the intent of the originator of the thread. So the combo must be effective against multiple enemies.

Legacy + anyone does more damage, so his very presence is a combo. For a Legacy combo to be more "killer", it needs to be with the Heroes that use it to greater advantage.

For instance, Galvanize + Squall does baseline 2xtargets in damage. That seems like a killer combo against some villains, but not all. It is very effective against Infinitor's weak Manifestations, but bounces off Akash'bhuta when she's got lots of arms out or Apostate's Relic damage reduction. It is also contraindicated against Voss (because it tends to flip him) and Citizen Dawn (losing control of the Citizens in discard due to it being indiscriminate), but especially Dreamer since it kill sher and you lose. It is also no help against villains with very low villain target counts in the deck. So I can't call it killer. It is merely situationally more effective.

This differs from the standard AZ+Legacy combo. With his modules in play and Legacy giving +2, Thermal Shockwave heals AZ for 1+2x2 while dealing 2x(1+2) damage. It can instead deal AZ -1-2+6+2=5 damage, deal one target 1+2, and a second target (1+2)+(8+2) damage. Legacy's effects are dealt 4x to one target at the cost of 2x to AZ, which puts Fanatic to shame for her version of "hurt self to hurt others". It is flexible and can get even worse with a third target instead of healing. It even penetrates higher Damage reduction, which someone earlier commented about with reference to Fanatic's effect with Legacy.

Since I only just got WotC Thurs, I hadn't had a chance to experiment with the decks yet. CC and SS work extremely well in combination, but are not a killer combo. They cover each other's weaknesses extremely well, and raise reliability of victory vs. other pairings, but do not amplify each other. They fill each others' holes. SS, for instance, taking all damage from hero targets protects the constructs. And CC gives SS a way to do direct single target damage. There is a synergy there, but not a killer combo. SS seems a shoe-in as best combo with Unity. She also gets Legacy's Ring into play, which has always been Legacy's weakness. One of the best five card teams may wind up being Wraith+Legacy+Sky-scraper+Absolute Zero+Unity (in that order). Ongoing and environment destruction, lots of equipment to sacrifice, healing, Villain Deck control, villain damage reduction and control, and the raw damage AZ can flood out.

CC does have an effective combo that might be killer, but it is a healing combo, rather than damage. Vitality Conduit+Motiviational Charge + any ability that hits a Hero target for 1 damage (like Thermal Shockwave). Shockwave hits VC for 1, heals target for 2, later MC hits something for 2, heals everyone for 1 including the VC. Rinse and repeat. Further enhanced by Dynamic Syphon, which allows this to go off every Hero Turn for each Hero that can damage DS and VC. Killer? Since it works against almost every enemy, I'd say yes. But Legacy can't buff up damage anymore, or the Constructs die, so it is a post-near death recovery combo. Cosmic Crest helps with another DS on CC, but now we're getting into stupid numbers of cards. In our case, we had Tempest out, too, with Healing Rain, but I thought that was too much healing and was lengthening the game unnecessarily.

Nightmist + Tachyon + Visionary can combine well. They feed cards into each others' hands, and two make good use of them. (I look forward to Super Scientific Tachyon with Nightmist online with Relics, but quite a wait for that.) Much as I like Nightmist for her fun factor, she comes out soft far too often, and can tear herself up trying to become effective, then wind up unable to get herself healed back up fast enough to participate. Early on, this team has weak damage output and no healing except personal, so can wind up letting the enemy flood out. The weakest point is Visionary, who seems to die first every time.

Keeping track of Turns is not difficult. Take all the divider cards and stack them, top first (ie. Villain on top). When each turn ends, move the top of the stack to the bottom. I can play at work, but we all have to prioritize work and can rarely put our heads together. In order for each person to tell whose turn it is, just by looking and not interrupting others actually doing the job, they just grab the stack. If it is Villain or environment, anyone can do it, but if it's the first player, he can segue into Hero turns. If it is your Hero, then execute your turn and move through environment and villain if you're last.

A friend of mine wants to put damage on the divider, but if we need to keep track of turns, he doesn't get to.

awp832:

My favorite is probably  Fanatic + Ra

Embolden + Imbue Fire + Flesh of the Sun God lets Ra use 2 powers consistently every turn with no price tag, its pretty nice.

Was re-reading this thread, and spotted this combo. It does not work.

Embolden demands that "If they take no damage this way, destroy this card." Ra becomes immune to the fire damage dealt by Embolden, takes no damage this way, so the card is destroyed at the end of the first turn Imbue Fire is involved, and may only gets its use once. You can reduce that damage by 1 and still keep Embolden in play, but the Hero character must take damage. It cannot be redirected, either. Embolden works better on the Alien with Many Powers (Tempest of course) who can heal off the damage it causes with one Power use and damage with the other. Another example you can try easily online is Heroic Interception which makes Wraith immune to damage, so she takes no damage and Combat Stance will not activate.

Also note that Imbue Fire shuts down Sacrosanct Martyr, so Ra once again does not play well with others. The absolute nature of Imbue Fire (where the other players cannot say, "No, I do not want it's effect") makes for a strong desire for me to ban him from certain players with too self-centered a mind-set. The problem is, he is the strongest direct damage deck in the game, and such players want him for exactly that reason.

There are a couple other cards like that you have to watch out for. Damage Dealt effects (except for reduction) generally do not trigger unless real damage is dealt. As much as I want it to, Omnitron-X does not get to hit back with Reactive Plating Subroutine, unless he takes at least 1 point of damage after the relevant plating is subtracted from damage. RPS is not a method to kill all Matriarch's birds in one turn, for instance.

I do wish the designers would start using "takes damage" or "receives damage" more often instead of using the current context sensitive "dealt damage", but it's what we have to work with right now.

The absolute nature of Imbue Fire (where the other players cannot say, "No, I do not want it's effect") makes for a strong desire for me to ban him from certain players with too self-centered a mind-set. The problem is, he is the strongest direct damage deck in the game, and such players want him for exactly that reason.There are a couple other cards like that you have to watch out for. Damage Dealt effects (except for reduction) generally do not trigger unless real damage is dealt. As much as I want it to, Omnitron-X does not get to hit back with Reactive Plating Subroutine, unless he takes at least 1 point of damage after the relevant plating is subtracted from damage. RPS is not a method to kill all Matriarch's birds in one turn, for instance.I do wish the designers would start using "takes damage" or "receives damage" more often instead of using the current context sensitive "dealt damage", but it's what we have to work with right now.

Well if you have a jerk Ra who uses ill timed Imbue Fire, just pick DW Fixer and the problem solves itself.

I'm a bit astonished at the perception of Chrono as being a "weak" hero.  

My favorite combo with him is this:

Play hunter and hunted with no bounties out.  Play the Compounded bow, preferably by using a displaced armory.

Then, play "By any Means" and "The Ultimate Target", preferably by using his Ranger's Mark or the Sudden Contract.  

This should bring you up to 5,5 damage (to the target with both bounties, using the bow, and 3,3 to any other target), which can be further increased as you get out additional bounties or through the one shots.  In our games, its quite common for Chrono to get up to 6,6 or higher with the bow, with no outside help, and playing two (or more) cards that do additional damage. A standard chrono-ranger turn, after minimal setup (1-2 turns), is to do anywhere from 8-14+ damage on cards, then another chunk of damage through use of the bow. And this is completely discounting if he manages to get any chains going with eye on the prize, or terrible tech strikes. Also bear in mind that this is without any outside help at all- other people just make him better, especially against armored targets. 

Most of my friends have stopped using Chrono because he obliterates most enemies, and actually apologize when they want to play him because they feel like they will be taking the fun out of the game by ending it so quickly.

posts.cooked: Vis has nice card draw, and Ra has much better card draw than Legacy, who needs to find both cards, not only play them. Ra is far from shut down by using this strategy, since he still has a ton of powerful damage cards. All he is losing is his base power, and the loss of Galvanize can easily be more detrimental to the damage output than just the loss of Ra's power (especially with more players). Not too mention for several turns, Ra can use two powers if he really needs to. It's also worth pointing out that Ra has no downtime to be hit by things, since he is always immune to fire damage, while Legacy can get hurt on his turn. Does it have some disadvantages, sure, but from my experience, it is much easier to get into play, not to mention get back setup if the Ongoings are destroyed.
